pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A ruling explicitly deriving one article's content from the other (e.g. history-preservation as a precondition for identity continuity, explicitly argued) would upgrade this.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both are sibling articles of the same ratified constitution (Article 2 vs Article 11 of the same numbered-law document) -- the exact 'sibling articles of a ratified constitution' pattern explicitly flagged in the task instructions as producing correct UNWITNESSED verdicts. pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: Would be wrong if a later article explicitly derives the History Law's requirements from the Dimension Law's structure (e.g. history-tracking is itself framed as one of the dimensions).

pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row explicitly relating Authority Law and History Law (e.g. a ruling that authority provenance must itself be historically versioned, cross-referencing both laws by number) would supply direct evidence.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: Only evidence is STRING-SIMILARITY ('kos','law') plus shared rows S0239/S0240/S0241, which are the same large multi-law registry/catalog tables seen elsewhere (H-KOS/INV-KOS family) -- Article 4 (Decision Law) and Article 11 (History Law) appear as separate numbered articles in one constitutional-law catalog with no direct cross-claim.

pairs_touching.what_says_this: STRING-SIMILARITY ('kos','law') plus CO-OCCURRENCE (both appear as sibling articles in the eleven-law Constitution enumeration). No claim ties Article 6 (Verification Law) to Article 11 (History Law) beyond both being members of the same enumerated law list.

pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A clause conditioning History's non-overwrite guarantee on Unknown being a preserved (not-flattened) state, or vice versa, would establish real dependency between these two specific laws; not present in the rows checked.

Adjacent sibling articles in the same ratified constitution, not a lineage pair.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row stating the History law's revisability requirement was derived from or motivated by the Agency law's accountability requirement would establish a genuine dependency.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Result: only TWO of the five are fundamental architectural absences -- persistent epistemic identity and historical belief evolution
rationale_evidence.statement: LLM-comparison validation (5 candidates, validated not assumed): persistent epistemic identity -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (a stateless generative model cannot possess it by construction; scaffolding like RAG cannot grant identity, only look up stored identities); historical belief evolution -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (generation is stateless, no belief to evolve); provenance preservation, contradiction management, justification accountability -- each a DEGRADATION, not an absence (an LLM can be scaffolded to approximate each, weakly). Conclusion: the constitutional justification rests on exactly the two fundamental absences (mapping to laws 1 and 11), not a general 'LLMs are bad at X' claim.
